content:
Subtraction trips up more Class 1 children than any other topic, mostly because of borrowing and the "how many more" wording. Here is what the Olympiad tests, the handful of facts that fix most errors, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 1 Subtraction Olympiad tests

  • Taking away and finding how many are left
  • Two-digit subtraction, with and without borrowing
  • Missing-number sentences like ▢ − 4 = 6
  • Word problems using "left", "fewer" and "how many more"

Key facts your child should know

  • Taking away 0 changes nothing (8 − 0 = 8); taking a number from itself gives 0 (8 − 8 = 0).
  • Subtract the ones first, then the tens; borrow a ten when the top ones digit is too small.
  • Check any subtraction by adding back: if 12 − 5 = 7, then 7 + 5 should be 12.
  • "How many more" is a subtraction: the bigger amount minus the smaller.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Subtracting the smaller ones digit from the larger regardless of position — doing 34 − 19 as 9 − 4 in the ones.
  • Forgetting to reduce the tens digit after borrowing.
  • Reading "how many more" as an addition.

quiz.title: IMO Class 1 Subtraction Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: Count back from 15: take away 8 and you land on 7. So 15 − 8 = 7.

questions.q: Gita has 53 stickers and Farhan has 26 stickers. How many more stickers does Gita have than Farhan?
Take the smaller number from the bigger number: 19 and 53.
questions.explanation: The bigger number is 53 and the smaller is 19. 53 − 19 = 34.

questions.q: There were 32 birds on a tree. First 15 flew away, then 6 more flew away. How many birds are still on the tree?

questions.explanation: Add back what was taken away: 26 + 30 = 56. Check: 56 − 26 = 30.

questions.q: Take the smaller number from the bigger number: 34 and 61.
questions.explanation: The bigger number is 61 and the smaller is 34. 61 − 34 = 27.

questions.q: How many must be added to 28 to make 50?
questions.explanation: Find the jump from 28 up to 50: 50 − 28 = 22.

questions.q: Meera picked 55 flowers. She gave 23 to her mother and 14 to her teacher. How many flowers does she have left?

faq.a: When the top ones digit is smaller than the bottom one, you take one ten from the tens column, turning it into 10 extra ones so you can subtract.

faq.q: How can a child check a subtraction?
faq.a: Add the answer back to the number taken away. If it returns the starting number, the subtraction is right.
